summary: Big Ridge tower site, Alleghany County VA: once overlooked Sweet Chalybeate and Sweet Springs; registered 2018; listed gone; no build or staffing source found.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone on the Forest Fire Lookout Association county list; no source describes what, if anything, remains at the site

events.note: Registered July 30, 2018, nominated by Kristin Reynolds (US 1722, VA 24)

evidence.supports: tower site atop Big Ridge overlooked Sweet Chalybeate Springs and Sweet Springs
evidence.quote: Located atop Big Ridge, this site overlooked the famed historic springs resorts of Sweet Chalybeate Springs and Sweet Springs.

evidence.supports: administered by the U.S. Forest Service
Big Ridge is in Alleghany County
located in the George Washington National Forest
county list marks the Big Ridge tower as gone

evidence.quote: developed in 1836 into a commercial resort, which lasted until 1918

notes_for_editor: Thin record. The story names the register as the Former Fire Lookout Sites register, the title on the firetower.org page; the Forest Fire Lookout Association appears there only as a sister-site link. The Forest Lookouts Big Ridge page has only the county and forest header, with no station text, build date, or history. The register supplies the overlook description, elevation, administering agency, and registration. Status gone is from the county list. Two WebSearch queries returned no history for this tower; the Sweet Chalybeate Springs Wikipedia page does not mention a lookout. The DHR page on the springs resort (cited for the 1836-1918 resort dates) also does not mention a lookout; it is cited only for resort context. Next checks if wanted: Alleghany County newspapers, Virginia Department of Forestry records, and a direct NHLR listing (the nhlr.org address returned 404 when tried). The story is short because the sources have nothing more; it omits build, staffing, and fire history rather than describing their absence.
